questions.question: Which locator is the best first choice for a Save button?
questions.explanation: Role and accessible name describe what a user perceives, so the locator keeps working when classes or layout change.

questions.question: A locator matches three elements and the test calls `click()` on it. What happens?
options: The action throws a strict mode violation
The test waits until only one element matches, then passes
questions.explanation: Locators are strict, so an action on an ambiguous locator throws. Narrow the locator so it matches one element.

questions.question: Which CSS fallback is the least brittle?
questions.explanation: A stable attribute says what the element is. The other selectors encode page structure, which breaks when the layout changes.

questions.question: A test is flaky because a message appears after a slow request. What is the best fix?
questions.explanation: Web-first assertions retry until they pass or time out, so the test waits only as long as the page needs.

questions.question: When is `getByTestId()` the right choice?
options: For every element, because test ids never change
When nothing user-facing is stable enough to locate by
Only for elements inside an iframe
When an element has a visible label
questions.explanation: Test ids are a last resort among the `getBy*` locators, because users never see them and they say nothing about accessibility.
